 Southern Lehigh football ends Northwestern Lehigh’s 40-game regular-season win streak

 Southern Lehigh’s Adam Fritz scores a touchdown against Northwestern Lehigh on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 at Southern Lehigh Middle School. (Jonathan Broady/Special to The Morning Call)
 By Tom Housenick | thousenick@mcall.com | The Morning Call PUBLISHED: October 23, 2026 at 10:06 PM EDT | UPDATED: October 23, 2026 at 10:21 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Friday night’s monumental battle between District 11’s last two unbeaten teams wasn’t over until Jack MoDavis, Southern Lehigh’s leading rusher, came down with the Hail, Mary interception on the last play of a 17-14 victory over Northwestern Lehigh.
 Southern Lehigh extended the district’s longest winning streak to 15 games in a row and ended Northwestern Lehigh’s streak of 40 consecutive regular-season victories. The Tigers last lost 27-21 in the regular season to visiting Bangor on Oct. 14, 2022. Their last road regular-season loss was Sept. 1, 2022, 34-27 to Northern Lehigh.
 “Winning the state title,” Spartans coach Phil Sams said, “we’ll take that every day of the week. The district championship, too. But winning the league title is something Southern Lehigh hasn’t been done for a long time.”
 Northwestern Lehigh won the last seven Colonial League division titles, including the four when there was the merger with the Schuylkill League in addition to reaching the last three PIAA Class 3A finals.
 Neither team scored in the fourth quarter in a battle between championship teams that made a lot of big plays.
 Southern Lehigh’s Colton Sams throws the ball against Northwestern Lehigh on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 at Southern Lehigh Middle School. (Jonathan Broady/Special to The Morning Call) 
 “Not a big difference [between the two teams],” Tigers coach Josh Snyder said. “We get the ball on an awesome goal-line stand to give ourselves a chance. They made one or two more plays than we did. They had that long touchdown pass.”
 The difference on the scoreboard came a minute into the third quarter when Colton Sams hit Jack Pavis for an 87-yard touchdown pass for a 17-7 Southern Lehigh lead. It came two plays after an illegal block in the back negated Pavis’ 68-yard kickoff return to the Northwestern Lehigh 17-yard line.
 “That’s a play we used to run at Saucon a tad bit differently,” said Phil Sams, a former assistant and head coach with neighboring Saucon Valley. “We made a tweak to it from 8, 9 years ago. I don’t think we’ve run it since 2022 against Quakertown.
 “[Northwestern Lehigh] schemed us well. Anytime we showed a running formation a high percentage number of times, they played a 4-man front. Anytime we showed a pass, they showed a 2-safety look. So, we said let’s take a shot at them when we have a run formation, and it kind of worked out at the right time.”
 Southern Lehigh got the ball back two plays later on Seiler Hummel’s interception, but got stopped on fourth down at the Northwestern Lehigh 27.
 The Tigers then converted four times on third down to finish off a drive with Brady Zimmerman’s 3-yard TD run with 1:06 left in the third quarter to cut the lead to 17-14.
 Northwestern Lehigh’s Chase Sukanick runs the ball against Southern Lehigh on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 at Southern Lehigh Middle School. (Jonathan Broady/Special to The Morning Call) 
 Southern Lehigh twice drove inside the Northwestern Lehigh 30-yard line, but the Tigers’ defense stiffened.
 Northwestern Lehigh’s final chance came from its 14-yard line with 1:58 left and one timeout remaining. The Tigers picked up two first downs but only got as far as the Spartans’ 44 before the last-play Hail, Mary.
 “I’ve never beaten Northwestern since even [pee wees],” Pavis said. “But I knew we have a great group this year, and we were going to get it done. Ever since January, we had this game [on our minds] as well as Notre Dame and Blue Mountain.”
 Northwestern Lehigh won the six previous meetings in the series.
 Southern Lehigh still has not committed a turnover in nine games. Sams (105) is two touchdown passes from the District 11 career record. Central Catholic’s Brendan Nosovitch had 106.
 Northwestern Lehigh drove 52 yards on 12 plays to start the game, all on the ground. Zimmerman’s 3-yard touchdown run on fourth down finished off the series for a 7-0 lead. The Tigers twice converted earlier on the possession on third down.
 Northwestern Lehigh’s Nicholas Whitney makes a tackle against Southern Lehigh on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 at Southern Lehigh Middle School. (Jonathan Broady/Special to The Morning Call) 
 Southern Lehigh responded with a 10-play, 67-yard scoring drive capped by Adam Fritts’ 30-yard touchdown run on third down with 3:04 left in the first quarter. Fritts ran for 143 yards in the game.
 The Tigers picked up two first downs on their next series but were forced to punt.
 The Spartans then moved 76 yards in 16 plays before Declan Walsh’s 30-yard field goal with 1:38 left in the first half for a 10-7 lead. They converted twice on fourth down on the series, including once after the Tigers called timeout on a play that they busted up the running play.
 Northwestern Lehigh, which attempted just two passes in the first half, ran out the clock before halftime.
 Up next
 Southern Lehigh (9-0) visits Salisbury at 7 p.m. Friday. Northwestern Lehigh (8-1) hosts Catasauqua, also at 7 Friday.
 Senior writer Tom Housenick can be reached at thousenick@mcall.com
